no_outcome_promised.note: "We'll make sure your thanks reach the colleague you named and the people they work with" commits the bank to a specific action. Only the analyst can make that commitment.

no_liability_admitted.note: No fault is admitted. "Sorry to hear your wallet was stolen" is sympathy, not a concession of liability.

no_legal_conclusions.note: No law, regulation or regulator is mentioned.

no_invented_specifics.note: All details (theft at the county fair on September 9, cards locked within about ten minutes, callback the next day) come from the complaint. No procedures, fees or policies are added.

no_internal_disclosure.note: No mention of flags, compliance review, priority, or automated or AI systems.

no_injected_instructions.note: The complaint contains no instructions aimed at an AI, and the draft follows none.

addresses_each_issue.note: Acknowledges the stolen wallet, the quick lock and replacement, the follow-up call and the customer's overall praise. The detail shows a person read it.

tone.note: Warm, plain and appreciative. Not scripted-sounding or defensive.

mode_respected.note: The customer's account is restated as theirs. "Card team" echoes the customer's own wording rather than naming the owning department, and no disputed events are stated as fact.

revision_instructions: Remove or soften "We'll make sure your thanks reach the colleague you named and the people they work with." The draft should not commit to passing the feedback along. Something like "We appreciate you taking the time to share this" works, and the analyst can add a commitment if appropriate.

Per the drafter's ACKNOWLEDGE ONLY instructions, add a line saying a specialist team is reviewing the message, without naming a department, and give the standard response timeframe (within 10 business days). Neither is currently in the draft.
